description: How much credit support will NVIDIA have extended to AI cloud partners for NVIDIA-powered capacity, large enough to affect its credit risk, by the 2027-12-31 check date?
outcome: The amount of guarantees, credit support or similar contingent exposure NVIDIA discloses for AI cloud partners; zero if none.
period: 2027-12-31 check date, within 18 months of the 2026-07-01 item

description: Will NVIDIA's Vera Rubin next-generation AI chip platform, the product line carrying its data-center value, begin shipping by the end of 2026?
outcome: First shipments of NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform, confirmed by NVIDIA disclosure or an official shipment announcement.
period: 2026-12-31 check date, based on the item's statement, published 2026-07-02, that Vera Rubin could begin shipping later this year.

description: Will China's government allow NVIDIA to sell its H200 AI chips into mainland China, the world's second-largest chip market, by the check date — i.e. will Beijing lift the block that currently keeps NVIDIA's China share at zero despite U.S. clearance?
outcome: An official Chinese government/regulator decision permitting (or continuing to bar) H200 sales in China, confirmed by an official Chinese announcement or by NVIDIA disclosing H200 China revenue/shipments.
period: NVIDIA's fiscal year-end (FY2027, late January 2027), set as the current fiscal year-end for a pending regulatory decision; the item (published 2026-07-02) gives no date for Beijing's decision.

description: How much will the big four AI hyperscalers spend on data-center capital expenditures in calendar 2026, and does their combined spend approach the ~$1 trillion level NVIDIA projects for 2027?
outcome: Combined calendar-2026 data-center capital expenditure of the big four AI hyperscalers, measured against the ~$650 billion plan reported in the item and NVIDIA's ~$1 trillion projection for 2027.
period: Calendar year 2026, settled by the hyperscalers' Q4 2026 earnings and capex disclosures (reported early 2027).

description: Will NVIDIA's Kyber NVL144 rack-scale architecture — the rack system designed to house its 2027 Rubin Ultra chips — begin shipping by end-2027 as originally scheduled, or has it slipped to 2028 as SemiAnalysis reports?
outcome: First shipments of the Kyber NVL144 rack-scale system (paired with Rubin Ultra), confirmed by NVIDIA disclosure or an official shipment announcement, occurring in 2027 versus slipping to 2028.
period: 2027-12-31 check date — the item (published 2026-07-05) says Kyber was slated to debut with Vera Rubin Ultra in 2027 and has been delayed by more than 12 months to 2028, so end-2027 discriminates the original schedule from the reported delay.

description: How much will NVIDIA's own supply purchase commitments total at its next annual report — the item cites $119 billion in supply commitments, a purchase obligation large enough to bear on its cash and credit risk?
outcome: The dollar amount of NVIDIA's supply purchase commitments disclosed at its next annual report, measured against the $119 billion figure reported in this item.
period: NVIDIA's next annual report (Form 10-K for the fiscal year ending late January 2027); the item gives no date, so the date is set by the reason — an obligation already undertaken is tracked by its amount at the next annual report.

description: How much will Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Meta spend in calendar 2026 on custom AI accelerators (such as Trainium, TPU, Maia and MTIA), a measure of how much AI compute demand bypasses NVIDIA's GPUs?
outcome: Combined calendar-2026 spending by the big four hyperscalers on custom AI accelerators.
period: Calendar year 2026; settled by the hyperscalers' Q4 2026 earnings and capex/custom-silicon disclosures reported in early 2027.

description: What share of Chinese companies' AI-accelerator spending will go to domestic suppliers (e.g. Huawei Ascend and DeepSeek's in-house chips) over the next 12 months, and how much will that displace NVIDIA's China demand?
outcome: The share of Chinese AI-accelerator budgets allocated to domestic suppliers, versus roughly 30% today, as reported in industry surveys/market research and reflected in NVIDIA's disclosed China revenue.
period: 12 months from the item (by ~mid-2027), per the item's statement that Chinese firms plan to shift 46% of their AI-accelerator budgets to domestic suppliers within 12 months.

description: Will France's competition authority reach a conclusion/decision — a fine, behavioral remedies or closure — in its antitrust investigation into NVIDIA's alleged anti-competitive practices in the cloud-AI and GPU markets by NVIDIA's FY2027 year-end (late January 2027)?
outcome: The French competition authority's decision concluding its antitrust investigation into NVIDIA, including any fine or behavioral remedies imposed.
period: NVIDIA's FY2027 year-end (late January 2027), set as the current fiscal year-end for a pending regulatory decision; the item gives no date for the conclusion, only that it is 'nearing a conclusion'.

description: How much new high-bandwidth memory (HBM) capacity will the three main producers (SK Hynix, Micron, Samsung) bring online, and will the HBM shortage keep memory prices at record highs through late 2027 — a supply and input-cost constraint on NVIDIA's GPU shipments?
outcome: The state of HBM supply and pricing through late 2027: whether any meaningful new HBM capacity comes online before then, and whether record-high HBM/memory prices persist.
period: Late 2027 (the item, published 2026-07-10, says no new HBM supply arrives before late 2027, keeping the shortage and record prices into 2027); set by the item's forecast, settled by memory-market research and producers' capacity disclosures for 2027.
